A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAPO algorithm and Rewarped simulation platform. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the additional appendix material in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original policy-training experiments on Rewarped and DFlex tasks, component ablations, and simulator runtime measurements in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports algorithm training times and policy loss-surface analyses in Appendices F.5 and F.7.

M1.justification: SAPO's objectives, entropy adjustment, policy parameterization, critic ensemble, and optimization choices are unchanged. Algorithm 1, the visual encoders, and Rewarped's simulation procedures are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six Rewarped tasks and four DFlex locomotion tasks. The added timing and loss-surface analyses reuse HandFlip and DFlex Ant; they introduce no new task, population, or environment condition.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain PPO, SAC, APG, SHAC, and, for Rewarped evaluation, TrajOpt. The new timing and loss-surface comparisons reuse existing methods without changing comparator membership in the retained experiments.

E3.justification: Appendix F.7 adds evaluation of final-policy perturbations along two filter-normalized random parameter directions, using undiscounted episodic returns and symlog visualization. Training runtime is additionally compared in Table 18; the existing six-million-step HandFlip budget and other benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.7 examines local optimization-landscape smoothness for APG, SHAC, and SAPO on two existing tasks. Appendix F.5 also extends computational-cost analysis with algorithm training times. All earlier component ablations and scalability analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts, 95% confidence intervals, and simulator-timing averaging procedures are unchanged. Table 18 reports mean runtimes using the existing 10-seed experimental scheme, without introducing a new uncertainty estimator or reporting increased replication.

E6.justification: Table 18 adds HandFlip training times of 1.46, 1.67, 7.43, 7.66, and 7.77 hours for PPO, SAC, APG, SHAC, and SAPO, respectively. Tables 16–17 add derived relative-speedup entries, and F.7 reports visually flatter and smoother SAPO surfaces. Existing returns, simulator FPS, and memory values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The RL formulation, SAPO derivations, simulation equations, and task definitions are unchanged. The new loss-surface analysis is empirical and introduces no theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about maximum-entropy analytic policy optimization, parallel differentiable multiphysics simulation, and improved sample efficiency and task performance under equal environment-step budgets.

C2.justification: The added training-runtime discussion qualifies its measurements by noting that further optimization using PyTorch compile and CUDA graphs was not implemented. Existing interpretations of entropy regularization, HandReorient failures, and limitations of simulation-derived observations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-site pointer, removes v1's explicit promise to release all code upon publication, and discloses training times and unused runtime-optimization options. Existing hardware and hyperparameter details remain. The PDFs alone do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. PODS changes from Mora to Zamora attribution, the Lillicrap reference changes from preprint to conference metadata, and several author lists are corrected; these do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header, adds acknowledgments and Appendix F.7, removes the reproducibility statement, and makes limited reference and cross-reference edits. The main narrative and section organization remain largely identical.

P2.justification: v2 adds training-runtime Table 18 and loss-surface Figures 12–13, expands Tables 16–17 with relative-speedup columns, and shades SAPO rows in Tables 2 and 13. Existing plots and trajectory images are preserved, with limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The new training-time comparison makes computational costs clearer alongside the retained sample-efficiency results, while Appendix F.7 adds limited diagnostic evidence about optimization smoothness. These are useful, bounded gains. The loss-surface plots lack numerical axes and their textual figure references are reversed, limiting the added analysis, but the original method and experimental evidence remain intact.
